flags.reason: Health warning without permission after participant expressed doubt; raises resistance.
Verbatim repeat of line 12 ignores participant's response; pattern repeats at lines 31, 35, 43, 46.
Pressure to follow through ('Once you decide...') instead of exploring participant's own motivation.
Reframes goal as 'getting your life back' without reflecting participant's stated view; missed change talk opportunity.
Summary cites 'the hard part was the rain', a barrier the participant never mentioned; correct before next session.

score.summary: Coach repeated the same blood-sugar script about six times, sometimes after the participant objected, and used warnings and pressure that Richard pushed back on. Richard still produced strong change talk (lines 27, 44, 55, 59), which the coach partly drew out with good open questions at lines 50, 56 and 58, and the goal was set collaboratively.
strengths: Line 54: complex reflection named Richard's ambivalence well ('You're weighing it up, and that's fair').
Line 37: open question 'What do you think the next step should be?' elicited his own plan (line 38).
Line 50 and 56: open questions about why it matters and what feels doable drew out his energy and father-related motivation (line 55).
coaching_tips: Lines 12, 24, 31, 35, 43, 46: stop repeating the same information; after one offer, ask 'What would be useful to you?' instead.
Line 20: replace the health warning with a reflection, e.g., 'You're not sure this will last, and that worry makes sense.'
Line 60: summarize only what Richard said; the 'rain' barrier was not his.
Line 28 and 45 showed good autonomy support; keep this stance throughout and avoid following it with pressure.
Check feelings explicitly early in the call; the checklist item was skipped.
